Equality holds exactly when the walk is STRAIGHT -- every step the same direction, no turn and no reversal. The DEFICIT (speed above velocity) measures wandering: the reversed walk moves at full speed yet nets zero (velocity 0) -- motion without progress, which the ordinal count could not see and the metric makes precise. This is the metric structure's core.

value.definition: a_t = Delta^2 x_t = s_{t+1} - s_t (second difference of position)

steps.what: discrete acceleration -- the second difference Delta^2 (uniform motion <=> zero accel)
steps.why: the BUILDABLE half of acceleration, in the same discrete Mathlib-free style -- NO continuum. Discrete acceleration is the SECOND DIFFERENCE of position, equivalently the first difference of velocity: a_t = v_{t+1} - v_t = s_{t+1} - s_t, the change of step vector, a vector on the integer lattice. Its facts: (1) a STRAIGHT walk (constant step) has ZERO acceleration everywhere -- uniform motion, the discrete Newton's-first-law, and exactly 8.4's 'equality iff straight' seen locally; (2) acceleration is nonzero exactly at a TURN or REVERSAL and LOCALIZES the bend -- the elbow's accel is (0,0),(-1,1),(0,0): zero on the straight segments, nonzero only at the corner; (3) a REVERSAL is the maximal single acceleration, |a|^2 = 4 (a full 180-degree flip of the unit step); (4) the accelerations TELESCOPE: their sum is v_last - v_first, the net change of velocity over the walk. All exact integer-lattice differences -- the discrete increment, with the continuum left emergent (8.6).
